sliceReports.summary: Completed the slice-3 test suite for the exhaustive semantic types and standardized SVG icons. Added characterization and requirement tests for all 47 built-in types (28 new), providers/config precedence, defaults, ZestIcon reuse/performance, accessibility, security, and the existing-19 compatibility guard, plus a toggle/type-icon coexistence regression. The tests exposed one genuine R3 sizing gap: raw built-in SVG icons used directly as iconLeft were outside the .zestIcon wrapper, so they fell back to the browser's default SVG size. Added width/height 1em to the shared iconBaseProps in UI/zestIcons.tsx, which makes every built-in icon scale with the button's font size. Verified with npx tsc --noEmit, npm run build, and the full Jest suite (18 suites, 221 tests) all passing.

findings.description: R5 requires an unknown icon name to render nothing and not throw, and documentation/api.md and documentation/features.md promise exactly that. Because inherited Object.prototype keys are treated as built-in icons, a consumer passing an untrusted string (route param, API value) can crash the render tree or render a bogus empty icon. Guard with Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(ZEST_ICON_ELEMENTS, name) (or use a Map/null-prototype object) before indexing.
findings.evidence: getZestIconElement checks `name in ZEST_ICON_ELEMENTS`, which walks the prototype chain. Rendering <ZestIcon name="__proto__" /> through React 18 renderToStaticMarkup against the built dist/index.cjs.js throws "Objects are not valid as a React child (found: object with keys {})"; name="constructor" and name="toString" resolve to Object.prototype functions and render an empty <span class="zestIcon"> plus a React warning, while a genuinely unknown name ("not-a-real-icon") correctly returns null.
findings.note: UI/zestIcons.tsx:161 now guards the lookup with Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(ZEST_ICON_ELEMENTS, name) and returns null otherwise, so __proto__, constructor, toString, hasOwnProperty and valueOf are not treated as icons. __tests__/ZestIcon.test.tsx:68-80 asserts getZestIconElement returns null and no svg renders for those names; the full suite passes.

findings.description: The feature's non-functional performance requirement is that the built ESM bundle grow by no more than 15 KB; it grew by 15,912 bytes, exceeding the agreed size budget. Trim the icon additions (remove the unused duplicate icons, share one element for identical drawings such as export/download and import/upload, and drop the leftover comments) until the delta is within 15 KB, or record an approved budget change. Do not leave the requirement unmet.
findings.evidence: Building HEAD (126a067) and the current working tree with the same rollup config and node_modules in scratch copies gives dist/index.esm.js = 65,106 bytes before and 81,018 bytes after: +15,912 bytes (15.9 kB / 15.5 KiB). The requirements cap the growth at 15 KB, so the bundle is over by 912 bytes (15 KB decimal) or 552 bytes (15 KiB). The bundle is unminified, so the unused duplicate icon definitions and leftover comments are shipped verbatim.
findings.note: Fresh rollup builds from the same config and node_modules (scratch copies): baseline commit 126a067 dist/index.esm.js = 65,106 bytes; current working tree = 79,993 bytes; delta = 14,887 bytes, which is within the 15,000-byte (and 15 KiB) allowance. findings.description: R5 requires an unknown icon name to render nothing and not throw, but names that collide with Object.prototype (__proto__, constructor, toString, valueOf, hasOwnProperty) are treated as built-in icons. A library consumer that passes an untrusted string as ZestIcon name (for example a route parameter or API value) can crash the app's render tree (availability/DoS) or render a bogus empty icon. Use a null-prototype map, a Map, or Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(ZEST_ICON_ELEMENTS, name) before indexing.
findings.evidence: getZestIconElement checks `name in ZEST_ICON_ELEMENTS` (line 167), so inherited Object.prototype keys pass as known icons. A probe rendering <ZestIcon name="__proto__" /> threw "Objects are not valid as a React child (found: object with keys {})" under React 18; name="toString" returned Object.prototype.toString and rendered an empty <span class="zestIcon"> instead of null.
findings.note: UI/zestIcons.tsx:161 now guards the lookup with Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(ZEST_ICON_ELEMENTS, name), so inherited Object.prototype keys such as __proto__, constructor, toString, valueOf and hasOwnProperty fall through to null instead of being treated as icons. The shipped dist/index.esm.js contains the same guard. __tests__/ZestIcon.test.tsx covers those inherited names, and the ZestIcon plus semanticTypeIcons suites pass (70 tests, 4 suites).

findings.evidence: R7 requires documentation/examples.md to have three recipes: (1) an icon-only button with aria-label, (2) overriding a default icon, (3) using the icon in a custom control. Recipe 7 ("Reusing the Standard Icons", lines 332-358) contains only (1) at lines 347-351 and (3) at line 353. There is no example that keeps a built-in semanticType and replaces its built-in icon. Recipe 4's only built-in override (lines 196-199) changes delete.buttonStyle, and documentation/configuration.md:181-194 overrides delete.buttonStyle and confirmOptions only; neither touches visualOptions.iconLeft/iconRight. A search for semanticType together with iconLeft/iconRight across README.md and documentation/*.md returns no match, so the capability is not shown anywhere. architect-r1 also lists "overriding a built-in icon" among the documentation deliverables for this feature.

The override examples are pre-existing, but they are still part of the pages this feature rewrites and they currently show TypeScript an error. Annotate the config objects (`const appZestConfig: ZestGlobalConfig = ...`) or inline them so the recipes compile.
findings.evidence: The documented provider configuration does not type-check: when the `const appZestConfig = { semanticTypeDefaults: { delete: { buttonStyle: 'outline', ... } } }` snippet (examples.md:183-200, identical shape at configuration.md:181-197) is checked with `npx tsc --noEmit --strict`, `buttonStyle` widens to `string` and `<ZestButtonConfigProvider config={appZestConfig}>` fails with TS2322: `Type 'string' is not assignable to type 'ZestButtonStyle | undefined'`. Passing the object inline or annotating it as `ZestGlobalConfig` (or `as const`) fixes it. The pattern predates this change (it is present at 126a067), so this is advisory rather than a regression.

findings.description: Restore the original indentation so the diff only changes the version values.
findings.evidence: Lines 518-520 are indented four spaces while the surrounding statements inside the same `it(...)` block are indented six, e.g. `    expect(read("README.md")).toContain("toggleOptions");` sits under a block whose other statements start at column seven. The mis-indentation was introduced with the version-expectation update from 1.6.0 to 1.7.0; it is cosmetic and does not affect behaviour.

findings.description: Extend the R7 docs test to all seven pages and compare every features-table column against semanticTypeButtonConfigDefaults, and add the missing default ZestButton import to the configuration.md example. Advisory: the shipped table content currently matches the defaults and the broken named import that QA-2 reported is now guarded, so this is proof breadth, not a current requirement break.
findings.evidence: The docs-import test only reads README.md and documentation/examples.md (line 194) and only parses `import ... from 'jattac.libs.web.zest-button'` clauses; features.md, api.md, configuration.md and breaking-changes.md are not parsed, and the features-table test at lines 159-170 extracts only the first table column. Consequently an incorrect Icon, Variant, Button style, Icon side or Default behaviour cell, or a non-compiling example outside README/examples, leaves the suite green. One such example exists today: documentation/configuration.md:137 imports only `ZestButtonConfigProvider, ZestIcon` but the same snippet renders `<ZestButton>` at line 166 without importing it.

findings.description: The documented recipe for overriding a built-in type's default icon is missing from examples.md, so the feature's override path that R6/R7 promise is not shown where readers look.
findings.evidence: R7 requires documentation/examples.md to contain recipes for (a) an icon-only button with aria-label, (b) overriding a default icon, and (c) using the icon in a custom control. Recipe 7 (lines 341-355) covers (a) and (c), but no recipe combines a built-in semanticType with visualOptions.iconLeft/iconRight to replace that type's default icon. Recipe 4's built-in override example (line 197) only changes buttonStyle on 'delete', and its provider example (line 188) sets iconLeft for a custom 'publish' type, not a built-in default.
findings.note: documentation/examples.md now has the missing override recipe: the TOC lists it at line 16, the body heading '### Recipe 8: Swapping a Built-in Icon' is at line 363, the first example (lines 371-386) keeps zest={{ semanticType: 'search' }} and replaces the built-in icon with visualOptions.iconLeft: <ZestIcon name="filter" />, and lines 389-397 show the iconRight form for the end-icon types (next, view, details). The recipe states the local icon wins so the default is not added twice and the label still comes from children. The recipe is accurate against the implementation: useZestConfig.ts applies local zest props last (step 4), and semanticTypeButtonConfigDefaults.tsx places the defaults for view (line 101), details (line 108) and next (line 212) in iconRight. The red-first guard __tests__/ZestIcon.test.tsx:193-203 reads examples.md and asserts the recipe exists with semanticType, visualOptions.iconLeft, a <ZestIcon> and the iconRight case. Re-ran verification: npx jest --ci --silent = 18 suites / 225 tests passed; npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json = exit 0.
